item.title: Patman Political Engagement Project Information Session — Tue Sep 15, 5:30 PM — Sanford 223
item.description:
The Hart Leadership Program challenges students to practice the art of leadership in public life. Applications are now open for several experiential learning programs that aim to shape Duke undergraduates for reflective, ethical leadership. Our core programs involve training both inside and outside the classroom through experiential education, pedagogical preparation, reflective practice, a strong community of peers, and an aspiration to public purpose.
The Patman Political Engagement Project is a Fellowship opportunity open to third-year undergraduate students of any major who are interested in political leadership, broadly defined. Patman Fellows take a spring semester gateway course (PubPol 564: Democracy Lab), receive personalized one-on-one mentoring, and are awarded funding to support either senior thesis research or a politically engaged internship.
Applications are now open and an information session for Patman will be held on Tuesday, September 15th at 5:30 PM in Sanford 2

item.title: The American Revolution at 250: Historians Discuss the Many Worlds of 1776 — Tue Sep 15, 6:00 PM — Durham County Library
item.description:
In conjunction with The Declaration of Independence Display we invite you to join us for a special event!
Famously, in December 1773, over a hundred colonists snuck onto ships in Boston Harbor after nightfall, destroying chests of tea worth nearly $2 million today. Often portrayed as a local tax protest that helped spark a Revolution, this event raises all kinds of questions: How did others elsewhere in America and across the world see such an affair? Why were the protesters dressed as Native Americans? Where did all that tea come from in the first place?
The "Boston Tea Party" was just one example of the many ways in which the American Revolution was a global phenomenon, whose causes and consequences reached from India and China to Indigenous nations across the North American continent. Join us as Duke historians Adriane Lentz-Smith and Philip Stern launch a year of discussions on these many different "Worlds of 1776," in conversation with UNC historian Kathleen DuVal, Pulitzer

item.title: CDVS Workshop: Excel Power Query to transform and aggregate data — Wed Sep 16, 10:00 AM — Online
item.description:
When I need to convert a table from wide format into tall (unpivot) or combine two spreadsheets by matching rows based on a key column (JOIN/merge), I used to turn to Python, R, or OpenRefine. It turns out you can do both of these operations right in Excel using Power Query! In this workshop I'll lead you through a quick example using survey data, where I unpivot and merge both the text and numeric versions of responses into a single table that's ready for analysis and visualization. Plus, I will show you how to summarize data in a way that surmounts a limitation of pivot tables for visualization. This event is open to non-Duke participants.
Source: Duke University

item.description: Playing is the joy and satisfaction of touring, but it comes with the hard part — travel, the endless miles on a bus. With tongue stuck somewhat in cheek, Little Feat announces “The Last Farewell Tour,” which will begin in April 2026. It’s deﬁnitely not an absolute, never-gonna-play again statement. This wind-down will take several years to accomplish, and while it does, Feat will continue to perform and record as long as they are able. It’s a retirement from the travel of touring. Guided by a somatic therapist, you’ll be held in a space that supports you in cultivating safety, self-awareness, and compassionate presence through restorative yoga and embodied practices. The experience weaves together gentle movement, crystal sound bowls, live music, guided group hypnotherapy, a tarot reflection corner, a collective altar, and intentional time for witnessing and connection. Join acclaimed writers Alexis Pauline Gumbs and Richard J. Powell for a conversation celebrating the legacy of pioneering artist Alma Thomas and the enduring influence of Black artistry. Hosted on the closing day of All American: Contemporary Perspectives from HBCU Artists, the program brings Gumbs and Powell together in celebration of their new books, Primary and Colorstruck!. item.title: Swift Night Out (Charlotte) — Mon Sep 28, 6:45 PM
item.description:
Join NCWF, Mecklenburg Audubon Society, and NCWF Charlotte Wildlife Stewards Chapter to meet the most spectacular aerial insectivores, Chimney swifts. These birds spend almost their entire lives flying, hunting insects, and even bathing on the wing. Having lost much of their habitat to development, chimney swifts now rely on brick mason chimneys for survival. As the sun goes down and the swifts make their way home for the night, chat with local conservationists about chimney swift biology, behavior, and conservation. Discover their miraculous fall migration and observe swifts up close using scopes and binoculars. The night will culminate with the spectacle that is many hundreds of swifts chattering while swirling into a vortex before dropping into the chimney. Help us count the birds and contribute to their conservation efforts. REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Wildlife Federation
